expectation.question: What are the Python Programming course completion requirements?

trace.question_text: What are the Python Programming course completion requirements?

answer.body: To complete the Python Programming course, learners must submit all four graded labs, achieve at least 70% overall, and earn a Pass on the capstone project. The overall mark and capstone Pass are evaluated separately. If necessary, one capstone resubmission is allowed after written feedback. The completion record is shown in the LMS Results area after these conditions are verified by the course coordinator.

sources.content: PY-101 / SYNTHETIC COURSE LIBRARY Python Programming Course Handbook Completion requirements The conditions for course completion To complete the Python Programming course, submit all four graded labs, achieve at least 70% overall, and earn a Pass on the capstone project. The overall mark and capstone Pass are evaluated separately. A capstone resubmission is available once after written feedback. The completion record appears in the LMS Results area after the course coordinator verifies the conditions. EduEvidence AI / Synthetic demonstration material Page 4 of 4

PY-101 / SYNTHETIC COURSE LIBRARY Python Programming Course Handbook Course overview Purpose and learning outcomes Python Programming is a six-week foundation course for new programmers. Learners write and debug small command-line programs, organize code into reusable functions, and read structured files. By the end of the course, learners can test functions, handle exceptions, and explain their design decisions in a code review. The course uses the Python standard library and the LMS practice workspace. The course notebook contains examples and extension exercises. EduEvidence AI / Synthetic demonstration material Page 1 of 4

PY-101 / SYNTHETIC COURSE LIBRARY Python Programming Course Handbook Assessment and submission What to upload and where Graded labs account for 60% of the course mark. The capstone project accounts for 40% of the course mark. Submit each lab through the LMS Assessments area as a ZIP archive containing Python source files and a short README. A successful submission generates an LMS receipt. Upload the capstone to the Capstone submission slot. Include your Python source, test files, and instructions for running the project. EduEvidence AI / Synthetic demonstration material Page 3 of 4

PY-101 / SYNTHETIC COURSE LIBRARY Python Programming Course Handbook Modules and weekly practice A six-week learning sequence Weeks 1 and 2 cover variables, control flow, strings, lists, dictionaries, and the interactive Python shell. Weeks 3 and 4 cover functions, modules, files, exceptions, and debugging. Week 5 introduces unit tests and code review. Week 6 is the capstone workshop. Learners bring a working prototype and receive feedback on testing and readability. EduEvidence AI / Synthetic demonstration material Page 2 of 4

expectation.question: What is the minimum live-session attendance requirement?
required_facts: at least 75% of scheduled live sessions

trace.question_text: What is the minimum live-session attendance requirement?

answer.body: The minimum live-session attendance requirement is that learners must attend at least 75% of scheduled live sessions. Attendance for a live session counts only if the learner is present for at least half of its scheduled duration. Watching a recording does not count toward live attendance.

sources.content: LMS-001 / SYNTHETIC COURSE LIBRARY LMS Assessment and Attendance Policy Attendance requirements Live sessions and recorded participation Learners must attend at least 75% of scheduled live sessions. A live session counts when the learner is present for at least half of its scheduled duration. Watching a recording does not count toward live attendance. A learner may request a documented accommodation from course support. Attendance records appear in the LMS Attendance area within two working days of a session. EduEvidence AI / Synthetic demonstration material Page 2 of 3

LMS-001 / SYNTHETIC COURSE LIBRARY LMS Assessment and Attendance Policy Assessment review and support How to request a review Request an assessment review in the LMS Support area within five working days after the grade is released. Include the assessment name, the rubric criterion, and a short explanation of the issue. The support team acknowledges the request in the LMS. Requests for general learning support can be submitted in the same area using the Course Support category. EduEvidence AI / Synthetic demonstration material Page 3 of 3

LMS-001 / SYNTHETIC COURSE LIBRARY LMS Assessment and Attendance Policy Assessment submissions Receipts and late work Submit graded work through the assessment slot listed in the LMS. Keep the timestamped submission receipt as proof of delivery. For assignments marked eligible for late submission, a learner may submit up to 48 hours after the deadline. The penalty is 10 percentage points per 24-hour period or part thereof. If the LMS is unavailable, contact course support and include the error details before the deadline where possible. EduEvidence AI / Synthetic demonstration material Page 1 of 3
